<div class="intro-box">
<strong>What is this page?</strong> This is your one-stop shop for preparing your group project. It contains a <strong>week-by-week timeline</strong>, a <strong>document checklist</strong> with guidance on each document, a complete <strong>worked example</strong> study for reference, and <strong>blank templates</strong> you can download and adapt for your own project. Bookmark this page — you'll come back to it often.

📚 **Suggested readings for all projects** are available in the <a href="https://learn.gold.ac.uk/mod/folder/view.php?id=1795121" target="_blank"><strong>Project Articles folder on Learn.gold</strong></a>.
</div>

# Week-by-Week Timeline

Use this to track what you should be working on each week. Documents don't all need to be finished at once — the timeline shows when each piece fits in.

<div class="timeline-table">

| Week | Dates | Focus | Key tasks |
|:----:|:-----:|-------|-----------|
| **16** | 24–28 Feb | **Form groups & choose project** | Form your group of 4–5. Read the [Project Options](group-project-options.qmd). Agree on a project and design (between or within). Submit your **Research Plan** (Fri 27 Feb, 12 noon). |
| **17** | 3–7 Mar | **Draft documents & start materials** | Draft: Participant Information Sheet, Consent Form, Debrief Form, Participant Instructions. Start your Researcher Procedure and Stimulus Materials. |
| **18** | 9–13 Mar | **Finalise everything & practice** | **MCQ Exam** (Wed 11 Mar). Finalise all documents and stimulus materials. Complete Researcher Procedure. Practice running the study on each other. Submit Research Study Order Form. |
| **19** | 17–21 Mar | **Data collection** | Run your study! Collect data in the lab session. **EDS Assignment** (Fri 20 Mar, 12 noon). |
| **20** | 24–28 Mar | **Data returned & start writing** | Gordon analyses and returns data to groups. Start writing your Research Report. |
|  | | **Easter break** | Keep working on your Research Report. |
| | | | **Research Report deadline** (mid-late April — exact date TBC). |

</div>

# Document Checklist

Your group needs to prepare **9 documents** before data collection day. Click each one for details on what it is, who sees it, and tips for getting it right.

<details class="doc-card" open>
<summary>
<span class="doc-icon">📋</span>
<div class="doc-info">
<div class="doc-title">1. Participant Information Sheet</div>
<div class="doc-meta"><span class="tag tag-participant">Given to participant</span> <span class="tag tag-shared">Both designs</span></div>
</div>
<span class="chevron">&#9654;</span>
</summary>
<div class="doc-body">

**What it is:** A formal document explaining the study to potential participants *before* they agree to take part. Required for informed consent.

**Who sees it:** Every participant — they read this before deciding whether to participate. They keep a copy.

**When needed:** Draft by Week 17, finalised by Week 18.

#### Tips

- Describe the study in general terms — do **not** reveal your hypothesis
- Include: purpose, what participation involves, time required, risks/benefits, confidentiality, right to withdraw
- Keep the language accessible — no jargon
- The template has the standard boilerplate sections; you mainly need to customise the "purpose" and "what will happen" sections

</div>
</details>

<details class="doc-card">
<summary>
<span class="doc-icon">✅</span>
<div class="doc-info">
<div class="doc-title">2. Consent Form</div>
<div class="doc-meta"><span class="tag tag-participant">Given to participant</span> <span class="tag tag-ethics">Ethics requirement</span></div>
</div>
<span class="chevron">&#9654;</span>
</summary>
<div class="doc-body">

**What it is:** A checklist the participant signs to confirm they understand the study and agree to take part. A legal and ethical requirement.

**Who sees it:** Every participant signs one. You keep the signed copies securely.

**When needed:** Draft by Week 17, finalised by Week 18.

#### Tips

- You mostly just need to update the **study title** — the checklist items are standardised
- Make sure the study title matches across all your documents
- Print plenty of spare copies (aim for 30)

</div>
</details>

<details class="doc-card">
<summary>
<span class="doc-icon">📝</span>
<div class="doc-info">
<div class="doc-title">3. Debrief Form</div>
<div class="doc-meta"><span class="tag tag-participant">Given to participant</span> <span class="tag tag-shared">Both designs</span></div>
</div>
<span class="chevron">&#9654;</span>
</summary>
<div class="doc-body">

**What it is:** A document given to participants *after* the study explaining its true purpose, including the hypothesis and relevant theory.

**Who sees it:** Every participant — they receive this after completing the study.

**When needed:** Draft by Week 17, finalised by Week 18.

#### Tips

- Unlike the Information Sheet, you **can** (and should) reveal the hypothesis here
- Briefly explain the theory behind your study (e.g., dual coding, anchoring)
- Include the data withdrawal instructions and support service contacts
- Keep it to about one page

</div>
</details>

<details class="doc-card">
<summary>
<span class="doc-icon">🗣️</span>
<div class="doc-info">
<div class="doc-title">4. Recruitment Script</div>
<div class="doc-meta"><span class="tag tag-researcher">Researcher use</span> <span class="tag tag-shared">Both designs</span></div>
</div>
<span class="chevron">&#9654;</span>
</summary>
<div class="doc-body">

**What it is:** A short script your group uses to approach potential participants and invite them to take part.

**Who sees it:** Researchers only — you read or paraphrase this when recruiting.

**When needed:** Finalise by Week 18.

#### Tips

- Keep it brief and friendly — 3–4 sentences
- Mention: who you are, what the study involves (briefly), how long it takes, where to go, and any incentive (snacks!)
- Print several copies so multiple group members can recruit simultaneously

</div>
</details>

<details class="doc-card">
<summary>
<span class="doc-icon">📊</span>
<div class="doc-info">
<div class="doc-title">5. Data Recording Sheet</div>
<div class="doc-meta"><span class="tag tag-researcher">Researcher use</span> <span class="tag tag-shared">Both designs</span></div>
</div>
<span class="chevron">&#9654;</span>
</summary>
<div class="doc-body">

**What it is:** A table where you record each participant's data (condition, DV score, optional demographics).

**Who sees it:** Researchers only — you fill this in after scoring each participant.

**When needed:** Draft by Week 17, finalised by Week 18.

#### Tips

- Include columns for: participant number, condition (if between-subjects), DV score, and any optional demographics
- Include a **scoring guide** so all group members score consistently
- The template has tables for both between- and within-subjects designs — delete the one you don't need
- This is where your raw data comes from, so accuracy matters!

</div>
</details>

<details class="doc-card">
<summary>
<span class="doc-icon">🧪</span>
<div class="doc-info">
<div class="doc-title">6. Stimulus Materials</div>
<div class="doc-meta"><span class="tag tag-participant">Used in study</span> <span class="tag tag-shared">Study-specific</span></div>
</div>
<span class="chevron">&#9654;</span>
</summary>
<div class="doc-body">

**What it is:** The actual materials participants interact with during the study — word lists, images, passages, rating sheets, questionnaires, etc.

**Who sees it:** Participants (during the study) and researchers.

**When needed:** Draft by Week 17, finalised by end of Week 18.

#### Tips

- This varies hugely by project — see the [Project Options](group-project-options.qmd) for what your chosen project needs
- Make sure materials are matched across conditions (word frequency, difficulty, length, etc.)
- The example study uses word lists; your project might need photos, passages, anagrams, or rating scales
- Test your materials on each other before data collection day

</div>
</details>

<details class="doc-card">
<summary>
<span class="doc-icon">📄</span>
<div class="doc-info">
<div class="doc-title">7. Participant Instructions</div>
<div class="doc-meta"><span class="tag tag-participant">Given to participant</span> <span class="tag tag-shared">Both designs</span></div>
</div>
<span class="chevron">&#9654;</span>
</summary>
<div class="doc-body">

**What it is:** A clear, step-by-step sheet telling the participant exactly what they will do during the study.

**Who sees it:** Every participant reads this before the study begins.

**When needed:** Draft by Week 17, finalised by end of Week 18.

#### Tips

- Write in plain, simple language — no jargon or technical terms
- Use numbered steps
- Do **not** reveal the hypothesis or what you expect to find
- Keep it short — half a page is usually enough
- If your between- and within-subjects variants have different procedures, you may need separate instruction sheets

</div>
</details>

<details class="doc-card">
<summary>
<span class="doc-icon">📓</span>
<div class="doc-info">
<div class="doc-title">8. Researcher Procedure</div>
<div class="doc-meta"><span class="tag tag-researcher">Researcher use</span> <span class="tag tag-shared">Design-specific</span></div>
</div>
<span class="chevron">&#9654;</span>
</summary>
<div class="doc-body">

**What it is:** A detailed step-by-step guide for the researcher running the study. Includes exact wording, timing, and the full procedure.

**Who sees it:** Researchers only — this is your "recipe" for running the study identically every time.

**When needed:** Draft by Week 17, finalised by end of Week 18.

#### Tips

- Be extremely detailed — include exact words to say to participants (in italics or quotes)
- Include timing for each phase (study period, distractor, recall, etc.)
- Include the **checklist of materials** to prepare before testing begins
- Any group member should be able to run the study from this document alone
- You will need a different procedure document for between-subjects vs within-subjects designs

</div>
</details>

<details class="doc-card">
<summary>
<span class="doc-icon">🛒</span>
<div class="doc-info">
<div class="doc-title">9. Research Study Order Form</div>
<div class="doc-meta"><span class="tag tag-researcher">Submit to Gordon</span> <span class="tag tag-shared">Both designs</span></div>
</div>
<span class="chevron">&#9654;</span>
</summary>
<div class="doc-body">

**What it is:** A form listing everything your group needs printed or provided for data collection day.

**Who sees it:** You submit this to Gordon so resources can be prepared in advance.

**When needed:** Submit by **end of Week 18** at the latest.

#### Tips

- List every document and how many copies you need (err on the side of printing more)
- Include any special requirements (e.g., colour printing, speaker, specific paper size)
- Don't forget consumables: pens, blank paper for recall sheets, snacks
- Submit this early to avoid last-minute problems

</div>
</details>


<div class="section-header">
<h2>Worked Example: Concrete vs Abstract Words</h2>
<p>A complete set of documents for one study — use this as a reference for quality and format</p>
</div>

<div class="example-warning">
<strong>This is an EXAMPLE, not your project.</strong> The documents below are for the study "The Effect of Word Type on Recall (Concrete vs Abstract Words)". They show you what a complete, well-prepared set of project documents looks like. <strong>Do not copy these for your own project</strong> — use the blank templates further down instead, and adapt them for your chosen study.
</div>

**Study summary:** Participants study a list of words and then recall as many as they can. The IV is word type (concrete vs abstract); the DV is the number of words correctly recalled (out of 15). The study has both a between-subjects variant (different participants get different word lists) and a within-subjects variant (all participants study a mixed list; concrete and abstract recall scored separately).

### Shared Documents (used by both designs)

These documents are the same regardless of whether the group runs the between- or within-subjects version.
